verdict: Avoid new chilli-linked spice exposure in Guntur until China demand and local arrivals stabilise; lend only to branded, diversified processors with clean stock-and-receivable discipline.
title: Guntur Spices Processing & Trade: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Guntur runs on red chilli: farmers bring pods to mandis, traders and cold-store owners hold stock, and processors clean, grind, sort and pack for domestic brands and exporters. **Cash is made in the spread between seasonal buying (Feb-June harvest) and year-round selling, so the balance sheet is really a stock-and-receivable book, not a factory.** Rating work on a peer spice processor shows net working capital at around 45% of operating income as on March 31, 2025, improved from 51% in FY2024, with seasonal raw-material availability (February to June) forcing higher stock [9]. Utilisation typically peaks July to November, i.e. now, through the Diwali season [10]. So when a proposal lands, check the stock statement against the season, not against last quarter.

## What has changed now
**Two local reports say Guntur chilli arrivals have halved while prices held stable, and that China has slowed buying of Guntur chilli [1][2][3].** Treat these as local trade press, not audited data, and note two of the three are translated aggregator pages. Nationally, exports are down 5.7% Apr-to-date in USD [D], and Andhra Pradesh GST collections are -0.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D]. Against that, AP electricity demand is +18.1% Apr-to-date versus India +9.5% [D], which tells us cold-storage and processing activity locally is not collapsing. Peer results are the counterweight: Orkla India grew revenue 10.4% in Q1 with chilli and coriander inflation at 78% and 40%, and pricing contributed 11.4% of growth [6]; Q4 profit rose 107% to ₹73 crore [7]. **Branded processors are passing cost through; traders holding naked stock are not.**

## Where to grow
**Pursue processors with branded or export contracts, own cold-storage capacity and a demonstrated pass-through of chilli inflation [6], plus spice volumes growing over 10% as seen at Orkla [4].** Avoid pure mandi traders and stock financiers whose collateral is chilli whose offtake to China has slowed [1]. For any exporter, collect from customer the share of revenue from China and the current order book before sanctioning.

## How to grow safely
**Structure as cash-flow lending against stock and receivables with a drawing-power formula, not a clean limit.** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly GST returns, and quarterly stock audits; require the borrower to hedge or cap unhedged chilli inventory. Because working capital runs near 45% of operating income [9], size the limit to the seasonal peak, not the annual average. Ask for the FY2027 repayment and capex plan where the group has term debt, as peers carry ₹54 crore repayment and ₹15-20 crore capex in FY2027 [10].

## Early-warning signs
- **Weekly mandi arrival and price data (weekly):** arrivals staying at half of normal with flat prices [2][3] -> ask for updated stock ageing and reduce drawing power.
- **Monthly GST returns (monthly):** turnover falling below the AP trend of -0.2% [D] -> freeze enhancement, review limit.
- **Monthly export shipment data (monthly):** China-bound volumes not recovering [1] -> shift exposure to domestic branded buyers only.
- **Quarterly stock audit (quarterly):** stock ageing beyond one season -> demand sell-down or additional collateral.
